thread:
kai: Heads-up — after the model swap in eu-west1 we're seeing a spike of 503s for mlserv inference (customer: Atlas). Impacting ~12% of requests, started ~2m ago. Need an expedited patch and want to skip canary for eu-west1 only. Thoughts?
ops-bot: deploy-bot detected new release candidate rc-2026.03.20-47 for service mlserv. Canary plan: standard 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 30m. Manual override available. See: https://releases.redwood.ai/rc/rc-2026.03.20-47
maya: how confident are we in the fix? what's rollback criteria? skipping canary is high-risk.
kai: quick repro logs: 
```
ERROR mlserv handler.go:312 failed to proxy request: upstream error status=503 code=EPIPE
stack: ...
```
Root cause: race when inflight KV cache invalidation hits during model swap. Hotfix is a 1-line guard in cache invalidation path that prevents double-close. Unit tests + small sim pass locally.
laura: oncall here. we can fasttrack eu-west1 only, but need two approvals and a rollback plan. Suggest: 10m pause between 25% and 100%, monitor 5m windows.
devon: OK to approve skip canary for eu-west1 if we pin to rc-2026.03.20-47 and have auto-rollback if error_rate > 2.5% for 5m or 99p latency regresses >100ms. Which metrics to watch: errors/5m, 99p latency, retries.
annie: add safety: if we see a sustained increase in 5xxs for >3m, rollback automatically and alert pager. Also tag the deployment with "skip-canary:eu-west1" and note in release notes.
release-bot: NOTE: Canary-skip request requires two engineer approvals and an oncall ack. Approvals: 0/2, Oncall: pending. Use `/release approve rc-2026.03.20-47 --skip-canary=eu-west1 --reason="urgent Atlas impact"` to record.
shiv: suggested release note blurb: "mlserv: fix race during model swap that could cause transient 503s — fixes Atlas customer regressions". Keep it short.
kai: patch deploy command for ops: 
```bash
# pin image on eu-west1 pool
kubectl --context=eu-west1 -n mlserv set image deploy/transformer transformer=redwood/transformer:rc-2026.03.20-47
# annotation to indicate expedited
kubectl -n mlserv annotate deploy/transformer release.skip-canary="true" release.note="Atlas-impact; auto-rollback on 5xx>2.5%"
```
laura: approving skip-canary for eu-west1. /approve from oncall.
devon: approving; will watch metrics and have rollback ready.
release-bot: Approvals recorded: laura, devon. Canary-skip threshold met. Proceeding with expedited rollout in eu-west1.
ops-bot: deploy action: starting rollout rc-2026.03.20-47 -> eu-west1 (pool: mlserv-eu1, nodes: 6). Strategy: 10% -> 50% -> 100% but pausing after 50% for 10m per expedited policy.
ops-bot: deployment step: 10% -> ok (3 pods replaced).
ops-bot: deployment step: 50% -> ok (3 more pods replaced). Pausing 10m for verification.
kai: monitoring: errors down from 12% -> 1.1% at 50% and falling, 99p latency improved ~80ms.
devon: seeing traces show no retries and upstream success rates normalizing.
annie: auto-rollback rule armed: if 5xx rate >2.5% for 5m will trigger rollback.
ops-bot: resuming rollout -> 100% completed. All pods now on rc-2026.03.20-47.
ops-bot: post-deploy smoke: service health=GREEN, 5xx=0.6% (5m avg), 99p latency = baseline+15ms.
release-bot: release notes updated: "mlserv: fix race during model swap causing 503s; backported to rc-2026.03.20-47. Deployed to eu-west1 with expedited approval; rollback criteria: 5xx>2.5% (5m) or 99p latency +100ms."
shiv: thanks — can we create a follow-up ticket to add a unit test harness for multi-swap concurrency? I'll take it.
kai: noted, filing ticket RD-4217.
laura: oncall sign-off: monitoring for 30m then close incident. :thumbsup:
devon: marking this as "expedite:eu-west1" in release tracker and notifying Atlas success channel.
ops-bot: deploy annotation complete. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/incident/INC-2026-0319-77
release-bot: closing expedite thread. All set.
shiv: great job team. short retro item: make skip-canary runbook clearer. :thumbsup:
